title: GNSS-free gravity-aided navigation in a maritime field trial
source_type: Research preprint, not yet treated as peer-reviewed
source_title: GNSS-free quantum gravity-aided navigation and fine-scale marine surveying with a strapdown quantum gravimeter
claim: The authors report a maritime demonstration of gravity-map matching without GNSS observations in the evaluated navigation solution.
boundary: The result relies on a quantum gravimeter, reference gravity maps, inertial navigation and processing. It does not establish that a gravimeter alone can replace GNSS in general.

title: Marine absolute gravimetry using atom interferometry
source_title: Absolute marine gravimetry with matter-wave interferometry
claim: The authors report a shipborne demonstration of absolute gravity measurement using matter-wave interferometry, addressing measurement constraints in a moving marine environment.
boundary: The work establishes a demonstrated measurement approach under reported trial conditions, not a commercial model evaluation or a universal GNSS-free navigation capability.

title: Hybrid atomic and relative gravimetry in a field survey
source_title: Geophysical survey based on hybrid gravimetry using relative measurements and an atomic gravimeter as an absolute reference
claim: A published field survey combined relative gravity measurements from a CG6 with an on-site atomic gravimeter serving as an absolute reference.
boundary: This validates the reported hybrid survey configuration only. The atomic device is not assigned to any commercial instrument record without an explicit model-level identification.

title: Sicily absolute gravity and height reference network
source_title: The first absolute gravity and height reference network in Sicily
claim: A gravity and height reference network in Sicily used the named Scintrex CG-6 for measured gravity differences, vertical gradient work and transfers between stations.
boundary: The article describes a specific reference network and its documented field procedure; its findings are not a blanket performance guarantee for every CG6 deployment.
